title: The \(L^2\)-Cartesian Numerical Radius of Hilbert Space Operators
summary: Let \(\mathcal{H}\) be a complex Hilbert space, and let \(T=H+iK\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})\) be the Cartesian decomposition of \(T\), where \(H=H^{*}\) and \(K=K^{*}\). We introduce the \(L^2\)-Cartesian numerical radius \[ ω_2(T)=\left(\frac{1}{2π}\int_0^{2π}\|\cosθH+\sinθK\|^2\,dθ\right)^{1/2}. \] We study its basic properties and compare it with the classical numerical radius \(ω(T)\). In particular, we establish the sharp estimate \[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}ω(T)\le ω_2(T)\le ω(T), \] and establish lower and upper bounds in terms of the Cartesian parts \(H,K\).
